properties.name: A payload says whether the session reading it is alone on the graph
properties.rationale: THE ROOT CAUSE BEHIND EVERY SHARED-GRAPH FAILURE THEY REPORTED, in their words: A SESSION CANNOT TELL THAT IT IS NOT ALONE. Nothing in any payload reports concurrency, so every seat reasons as if solo and the output actively encourages it. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (fact:defect-rollups-became-fleet-numbers-without-saying-so): defects 42->6->5->12 and gaps 48->55->69 on one graph in one day by non-coordinating sessions, including a 5->12 jump delivered to a session that had done nothing; TWO BOSSES, one of them the reporter, attributed a global movement to their own change — in the flattering direction, which is the one nobody catches unaided. The reporter told the user '42 -> 6' twice as their own result. It was not. Their argument for this specific field: a seat seeing `attached: 7` CANNOT HONESTLY CLAIM A ROLLUP AS ITS OWN, so one number prevents the whole class. The alternative in force today is a hand-maintained fleet convention requiring every citation to be labelled FLEET or SCOPED — a discipline layered on a tool that could just say it, and by their own standard a defect routed around rather than fixed. NOTE THE MIGRATION HAZARD THIS ALSO NAMES: loop_status and graph_report read IDENTICALLY before and after `--shared`; only the MEANING changed, so every citation of those counts written before the migration is now subtly wrong and nothing says so.
properties.statement: Tool responses that report graph-wide state SHALL make concurrency visible — at minimum the number of currently-attached sessions, and ideally last_write_at and last_write_by — and rollups SHALL label themselves as graph-wide rather than leaving scope to the reader. Requested as the #2 fleet ask and as the single 'if only one thing changes' item by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-07.
